title: How do you use the 4Ps of marketing in a product launch case?
description: The 4Ps (marketing mix) for case interviews. The "What to offer" branch of a product launch. A checklist, a worked example and how to say it.
hook: The 4Ps (product, price, place and promotion) is a simple checklist for marketing and launch questions. Here is how to use it in a case, and when not to.
body:
When it helps

The "What to offer" branch of a product launch.

The checklist

Product

  • Features
  • Range
  • Quality

Price

  • Level
  • Discounts
  • Tiers

Place

  • Channels
  • Coverage

Promotion

  • Advertising
  • Sales force
  • Offers

An example

A drinks company is launching a low-sugar energy drink for students. Product: flavours students like, a can that fits a bag. Price: close to the big brands, perhaps with a multipack deal. Place: campus shops, supermarkets near universities, delivery apps. Promotion: sampling at freshers' fairs and social media. Notice that every answer depends on knowing the customer first.

How it sounds in an interview

Once we know the customer is students, I'd plan the launch around product, price, place and promotion, starting with where they actually buy drinks.

Example: launching a healthier snack

A food company wants to launch a protein snack in supermarkets. Product: test whether buyers prioritise protein, taste, portion size or allergen information. Price: decide a price that covers manufacturing and retailer margin while still looking reasonable beside alternatives. Place: select the channels where target customers shop, then check shelf access and retailer listing fees. Promotion: test which message persuades shoppers, rather than assuming "high protein" is enough.

Suppose the bar retails for £2.00 and the retailer keeps 30% of the selling price. The manufacturer receives £1.40. If production and logistics cost £0.90 per bar, the contribution is £0.50, before marketing, overhead and one-off launch costs. At £500,000 of incremental fixed launch spending, it would need about one million incremental bars to cover that spending, assuming the contribution remains £0.50. That makes distribution and repeat purchases as important as a clever advertisement.

The 4Ps are useful when the strategic decision to launch is already largely made. If the interviewer asks whether to launch, start with market demand, economics and the client’s ability to win before planning the marketing mix.
